text: The first car tires were not black. They were white!
Rubber is naturally creamy white, and makers added a white powder for grip.
But white tires wore out fast.
So tire makers mixed in carbon black, a fine black powder that is basically soot.
It makes the rubber tougher and pulls heat out of the tread, so tires last far longer.
Today, a tire can be up to forty percent carbon black.
So tires are not black for style. They are black because soot makes them last!
